notes: Profile: small engineering platform team (70 engs) building an IDE-first code assistant for JetBrains users (IntelliJ/PyCharm).
Primary ask: tight local completions + cross-repo semantic search. They want the plugin to work with an on-prem index for proprietary code.
They insisted: 'local dev loop must feel native — completions in <30ms for local edits'
Interest in pinning model versions per workspace + automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant for low-latency contexts.
Current stack: Kotlin/Java backend, Python ML infra, artifact store on-prem (NFS), internal auth via SSO (Okta).

POC scope agreed: 1) Redwood Private deployed in their staging VPC, 2) JetBrains plugin integration (Auth + streaming API), 3) local index ingestion (incremental), 4) end-to-end latency & cost measurement.
Indexed corpus: ~120M LOC across mono-repo + microservices; want delta indexing only (file-level diffs) to keep index warm.
Model preferences: open 13B-style quantized models for local completions; fallback to 7B quantized for ultra-low latency. Also want embeddings for cross-file search.
Security asks: bring-your-own-key (HSM/KMS) integration, audit logs for prompts & responses, retention config per project, and SOC2/ISO proofing for vendor selection.

Quotes from call 2026-02-14: 'If we can keep token cost predictable and latency under 50ms for 90th pct, we're in.', 'Need plugin to work offline-ish: degrade to local cached completions when network unavailable.'
Integration notes: plugin should call Redwood streaming endpoint with chunked responses; prefer gRPC or low-latency WebSocket; need example IntelliJ extension scaffold and auth token rotation sample.
Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay for reserved capacity if it guarantees predictable throughput for CI/IDE bursts (peak mornings and PR seasons).
Eval criteria: median completion latency, 95th perc latency under 200ms for multi-file searches, token cost per 1k completions, security checklist complete.
Legal/licensing: review required for on-prem bundle license + SLA for security incidents.
Internal champions: Head of Platform (Emily Zhao) and VP Eng (Marco Ruiz).
Decision timeline: POC -> security review -> procurement (targeting Apr 2026).
Short-term next: schedule installer call w/ infra on 2026-03-15, provide plugin sample repo and small-reference index script.
Misc: asked for feature: 'local cache of KV for completions across restarts' and 'version pinning per project config file (nimbleide.yaml)'.
